questions.prompt: Which concrete pipeline should the landing page sell first?
questions.description: This decides the hero, proof, pack contents, and CTA. The page can mention other future packs, but should sell one primary implementation kit.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Workflow Optimization Pipeline: cmux + NotebookLM + Obsidian + Codex/Claude Code. It is broad enough to attract practical users and specific enough to package as an implementation kit.

questions.prompt: Who should the page speak to first?
questions.description: This affects copy tone, examples, and pricing. Secondary audiences can still appear lower on the page.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Automation builders / AI power users who already use Claude/Codex/NotebookLM/Obsidian but lack a repeatable operating workflow.

questions.prompt: What should the first commercial CTA be?
questions.description: This determines whether implementation needs real checkout now or only a pre-sell/waitlist landing page.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Pre-sell / waitlist CTA first. Use this page to validate demand and collect buyers before building entitlement/paywall infrastructure.

questions.prompt: What price anchor should the landing page show?
questions.description: The page can frame this as founder pricing, expected price, or early access pricing.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Founder price $19, normal price $39. For Vietnamese copy, optionally show 299k-399k VND equivalent.

questions.prompt: What should be in scope for the first implementation?
questions.description: This keeps the first build narrow and avoids accidentally building a full paid content platform.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add one landing page, navigation/CTA entry points, bilingual EN/VI copy if existing guide parity is expected, and static pricing/pack sections. Do not implement auth, real checkout, entitlement, or gated content in this round.

questions.prompt: What visual direction should the landing page use?
questions.description: The existing VividKit site uses guide-oriented glass/card sections. This choice decides whether the landing page feels like a guide page, a product page, or an operating-system schematic.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Practical product page: dense, concrete, toolchain/pipeline focused, with simple system diagrams and artifact previews. Avoid generic SaaS hero fluff.
